title: Temple and Presence
blurb: Follow God's dwelling among his people from the tabernacle and Solomon's Temple to Christ's body, the Church, and the new Jerusalem.

steps.title: The tabernacle is filled
steps.intro: When Moses finishes the tabernacle, a cloud covers the tent and the glory of the Lord fills it. God's presence travels with Israel and guides the people on their journey.

quote.text: The anointing of the People was—a foreshadowing of Christ; their rod a mystery of the Cross; their lamb a type of the Only begotten; their tabernacle a mystery of your Churches; their circumcision a sign of your sealing.

steps.question: Where do you most sense God travelling with you rather than staying in one place?

steps.title: Solomon dedicates the Temple
steps.intro: At the dedication of the Temple, Solomon prays with outstretched hands and asks whether God can truly dwell on earth, since even the highest heavens cannot contain him. He asks God to hear his people's prayers toward this house.

quote.text: For, even when His angels hear us, it is He Himself who hears us in them, as in His true temple not made with hands, as in those men who are His saints; and His answers, though accomplished in time, have been arranged by His eternal appointment.

steps.question: What difference does it make to you that God is both beyond all places and willing to hear you?

steps.title: The river from the Temple
steps.intro: Ezekiel sees water flowing from the threshold of the Temple, growing deeper and bringing life and healing wherever it goes. The image looks ahead to the life-giving water of the Spirit.

quote.text: we certainly do not understand a fount of that water which is created, but the Fount of that divine grace, that is, of the Holy Spirit, for He is the living water.

steps.question: Where in your life or community is God's life flowing, and where does it seem to have dried up?

steps.title: Destroy this temple
steps.intro: Jesus drives the traders from the Temple courts and says, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.' John explains that he was speaking about the temple of his body.

quote.text: And why did He also say, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up?” For that which was destroyed, the same clearly He raised again.

steps.question: What does it change to think of God's presence as found in a person and not only in a place?

steps.title: You are God's temple
steps.intro: Paul tells the Corinthians that they are God's building and God's temple, because the Spirit of God dwells in them. He urges them to build carefully on the foundation, which is Christ.

quote.text: In a word we believe that, I do not say apostles and martyrs, but, all the saints and servants of God have within them the Spirit of God, according to this: “Ye are the temple of the living God: as God said, For I will dwell in them.”

steps.question: How would your daily choices change if you took seriously that you are a dwelling place of God?

steps.title: Living stones
steps.intro: Paul describes believers as fellow citizens with the saints and members of God's household. They are built on the apostles and prophets, with Christ as the cornerstone, into a holy temple in the Lord.

quote.text: The “Temple of the King” is the Church itself: it is the Church itself that enters into “the Temple of the King.” Whereof is that Temple constructed? Of the men who enter the Temple? Who but God’s “faithful” ones are its “living stones”?

steps.question: What part do you play in the building of your parish or community?

steps.title: No temple in the city
steps.intro: John sees the new Jerusalem and finds no temple in it, because the Lord God and the Lamb are its temple. God's presence is no longer limited to one building, and the city is lit by his glory.

quote.text: In thy own house thou wilt fear robbers; of the house of God, He is Himself the wall. Therefore “blessed are those who dwell in Thy house.” They possess the heavenly Jerusalem, without constraint, without pressure, without difference and division of boundaries; all have it, and each have all.

steps.question: What do you most long for in a life where God's presence is unveiled?
